title: Mean NCEP latent heat loss fell while buoy estimates rose between 2010–2019 and 2023–2025 at 19 tropical sites
abstract: We tested recent NCEP latent heat flux changes against PMEL bulk estimates from measured buoy weather. A fixed set of 19 Atlantic and Pacific sites has enough data to compare 2010–2019 with February 2023–December 2025. With calendar-month adjustment, NCEP-minus-buoy flux error falls by 20.1 W m-2 in R1 and 30.3 W m-2 in R2. Conditional 95 percent bootstrap limits are -29.4 to -11.8 and -40.0 to -21.8 W m-2. Calibration on pre-2020 flux variations leaves changes of -16.2 and -27.5 W m-2. SST error falls by about 0.36 C in both products. A 25-day coverage rule and three baseline windows retain the sign. With equal calendar-month weights, buoy heat loss rises by 6.8 W m-2 while R1 falls by 12.3 and R2 by 22.8 W m-2. However, absolute flux accuracy improves: R1 mean error changes from +13.1 to -7.2 W m-2 and R2 from +31.2 to +1.3 W m-2; total error falls in both. This fills the independent flux-reference gap in earlier NCEP SST-error work and shows why absolute agreement cannot establish temporal accuracy. Small across-site SST/flux error correlations do not support assigning the full flux change to SST alone. Sparse coverage, bulk-flux errors, partly assimilated weather observations and no controlled model rerun limit causal claims. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: NCEP-minus-buoy flux and SST error anomalies at the selected sites. Curves are 12-month moving means of available monthly site means. Vertical lines mark prior SST input event dates, not fitted flux break dates. Site availability varies within the fixed set.
Absolute error falls despite a large negative change in bias. This separates temporal accuracy from absolute agreement.

citations.reason: Tests its NCEP flux-error claim with external buoy bulk estimates, while restricting causal and absolute-error interpretation.
Prior propagation of NCEP SST errors into GODAS motivates validation of the atmospheric flux.
